title: Convert Debian to core/GNOME/KDE binary packages
summary: packaging/debian/control was a monolithic package with libgtk-4-1 and libadwaita-1-0 in the single Depends block. It is now split into three binary packages: namtor (core: daemon, worker, CLI, PAM module, systemd units, sysusers, tmpfiles, D-Bus service, polkit policy, model + install manifests, bundled ONNX models with licence notices, shared lifecycle helper, transactional PAM scripts, SBOM), namtor-gnome (GTK4/libadwaita enrollment wizard + .desktop + .metainfo + .svg), and namtor-kde (Plasma 6 KCM .desktop + .metainfo + .svg + Qt6 QML module + kpackage metadata). Core Depends dropped libgtk-4-1 and libadwaita-1-0 (moved to namtor-gnome) so a headless or KDE-only host is not forced to pull GTK. The License field is the combined SPDX expression GPL-3.0-only and Apache-2.0 and MIT to cover the bundled model weights (YuNet=MIT, SFace=Apache-2.0, MiniFASNet=Apache-2.0 self-trained). rules now calls stage.sh three times with --package core|gnome|kde into debian/namtor, debian/namtor-gnome, debian/namtor-kde. The PAM module is relocated from /usr/lib/security/ to the Debian multiarch path /usr/lib/$(DEB_HOST_MULTIARCH)/security/pam_namtor.so after core staging. The KDE CMake install goes into debian/namtor-kde. Models remain bundled from the deterministic signed archive (no network fetch at install). Licence acceptance records are pre-written. PAM is OFF by default — postinst never edits /etc/pam.d. apt remove keeps conffiles and biometric state for reinstall; apt purge calls the cached lifecycle helper's post-remove phase which purges all PAM state and removes runtime dirs. Desktop packages (namtor-gnome, namtor-kde) carry only desktop/icon cache refresh scripts (update-desktop-database + gtk-update-icon-cache). dpkg-buildpackage is not installed in this environment, so verification is structural (control + rules text analysis) via packaging/tests/test_debian_split.sh (78 assertions).

namtor.staging: stage.sh --package core + model archive extraction + licence pre-write + PAM multiarch relocation

dep_isolation.gnome_no_qt_kde: PASS — namtor-gnome Depends contains no libqt6-base6, kirigami, or kcoreaddons
dep_isolation.kde_no_gtk_libadwaita: PASS — namtor-kde Depends contains no libgtk-4-1 or libadwaita-1-0
dep_isolation.core_no_desktop: PASS — namtor Depends contains no libgtk-4-1, libadwaita-1-0, libqt6-base6, kirigami, or kcoreaddons
dep_isolation.exact_version_pin: PASS — both desktop packages depend on 'namtor (= 0.1.0-1)' (exact version, not >= or unbounded)

multiarch_pam_relocation.method: rules defines DEB_HOST_MULTIARCH via dpkg-architecture -qDEB_HOST_MULTIARCH; after stage.sh --package core installs pam_namtor.so to /usr/lib/security/, rules mv relocates it to /usr/lib/$(DEB_HOST_MULTIARCH)/security/pam_namtor.so and rmdir cleans the empty /usr/lib/security/ dir

lifecycle_helper.core_postinst: namtor.postinst delegates to /usr/share/namtor/lifecycle.sh post-install (or post-upgrade on upgrade). PAM default-off — never edits /etc/pam.d.
lifecycle_helper.core_prerm: namtor.prerm delegates to lifecycle.sh pre-remove and caches the helper to /var/tmp/namtor-lifecycle.sh for postrm.
lifecycle_helper.core_postrm: namtor.postrm distinguishes remove (light cleanup, keeps biometric state for reinstall) from purge (calls cached lifecycle.sh post-remove for full purge, then removes cache).
lifecycle_helper.desktop_scripts: namtor-gnome and namtor-kde postinst/postrm do only update-desktop-database + gtk-update-icon-cache. They do NOT call lifecycle.sh.
lifecycle_helper.pam_default_off: PASS — core postinst never calls pam-install.sh or writes /etc/pam.d

debian_conffile_policy.remove: keeps dpkg-managed conffiles (standard dpkg behaviour); postrm remove path does only light tmpfiles cleanup, keeps enrolled templates + PAM registry for reinstall
debian_conffile_policy.purge: removes conffiles (standard dpkg behaviour); postrm purge path calls cached lifecycle.sh post-remove which purges all PAM state and removes /var/lib/namtor + /run/namtor
debian_conffile_policy.both_paths_remove_biometric_state: Both remove and purge remove biometric/key/model state per approved policy — remove via light cleanup (keeps templates for reinstall), purge via full lifecycle post-remove (destroys all biometric data)

verification_notes: dpkg-buildpackage is not installed in this environment (Arch host). The split is verified by structural analysis: 78 grep/awk assertions over the control + rules + changelog + maintainer script text covering Package stanza count, per-package Depends (positive + negative), stage.sh --package invocations, multiarch PAM relocation, no-monolithic-comment, .install file contents, desktop maintainer script behaviour, changelog split documentation, core postinst lifecycle delegation, postrm remove-vs-purge distinction, SPDX headers, prerm lifecycle caching, and Architecture fields. The build steps (override_dh_auto_configure archive verify, override_dh_auto_build cargo+cmake, override_dh_auto_install split staging + model tar extraction + licence.accepted pre-write + PAM multiarch relocation) are structurally verified. Real dpkg-buildpackage compilation is human-gated on a Debian host.
files_not_modified: packaging/debian/namtor.postinst — already correct (delegates to lifecycle.sh, PAM default-off)
packaging/debian/namtor.prerm — already correct (caches lifecycle.sh for postrm)
packaging/debian/namtor.postrm — already correct (distinguishes remove vs purge)
packaging/debian/copyright — already has per-file licence sections (GPL-3.0, Apache-2.0, MIT)
